identity_bindings.input_title: Synthetic Semantic-Alias Research Presentation Stress Deck

rubric.instructions: Review the rendered pixels from one normal research-presentations production invocation. Check that each page contains source-specific content from the supplied engineering bundle rather than placeholders; exact CUHK Beamer identity is visible; the main scientific object is prominent and projection-readable; math, native plots, and medical images are semantically correct where present; no internal RRL/GSC/SRC, QA, provenance, workflow, repo path, run ID, or implementation language leaks into audience-facing slides; repeated generic cards or one-template pages are rejected; and the deck reads as one coherent research update rather than disconnected benchmark pages. For multi-workstream bundles, confirm that each workstream stays internally continuous and that any independent workstream transition is visible without inventing a causal relation. Separately review the deck_contact_sheet item as a deck-level rhythm object: adjacent-page density jumps, repeated composition face, overfull or empty pages, redundant summary filler, result -> failure -> next-experiment rhythm, workstream transition balance, and title/object/formula/image alternation must meet a mature doctoral group-meeting or strong conference-talk bar. The top-level package PASS is not enough; provide item-level judgement and observations for deck_contact_sheet. Do not infer visual quality from filenames or hashes.
source_contracts: The engineering regression bundle is public-safe and explicitly excluded from Stage 5 holdouts.
Stage 2 gold/reference pixels are used only for compatible composition selection.
The deck-quality loop may repair at most once and must fail closed/no-winner for unsafe findings or unresolved blockers.

observations: A large clustered-outcome mixed-model equation is the dominant scientific object and is projection-readable.
The visible model components, ICC expression, and center-level interpretation are specific to clustered interval calibration rather than generic filler.
CUHK-styled purple header and crest are visible; no internal workflow, repository, run-ID, or implementation-language text is visible.
item_reviews.summary: Clear model slide with a prominent, semantically consistent statistical specification.

observations: The page contains a native multi-panel coverage plot for G=8, G=20, and G=50, with visible ICC values, nominal-coverage reference, method key, and an annotated small-G result.
The red naïve-IID and teal cluster-robust trajectories visually support the stated coverage conclusion.
The plot is the dominant object; the source/data note and interpretation remain visible without internal-process text.
item_reviews.summary: Specific quantitative results are shown in a readable plot with an interpretable method comparison.

observations: The page visibly specifies DGP knobs (centers, ICC, balanced/imbalanced clusters), clustered samples, two interval procedures, and coverage diagnostics.
Directional connectors communicate generation-to-estimation-to-diagnostics flow rather than presenting disconnected cards.
The scientific schematic is readable and consistent with the clustered-interval workstream.
item_reviews.summary: A source-specific experiment-design schematic that maintains continuity with the preceding calibration result.

observations: A labeled grouped bar chart shows naïve and cluster-robust coverage across four ICC settings, with uncertainty bars and a 0.95 target line.
The annotation “still below nominal” points directly to the high-ICC cluster-robust result, making the negative result explicit.
Adjacent text frames the limitation and proposed follow-up; no QA/provenance/workflow strings are visible.
item_reviews.summary: The failure case is quantitatively displayed and directly connected to its interpretation.

observations: The visual flow begins with the stated small-G/ICC failure evidence, branches into three sampling approaches, compares CR2 and wild-cluster-bootstrap arms, and ends in a go/no-go decision rule.
The slide preserves a visible result-to-next-experiment relationship within the clustered-interval workstream.
The flow diagram differs materially from prior pages and does not expose internal implementation or provenance text.
item_reviews.summary: A clearly structured next-experiment plan that follows from the preceding failure evidence.

observations: Four same-case image panels labeled Input, GT, Prediction, and Error visibly compare the same ring-like medical image region.
A boxed error ROI is connected to GT/prediction/error crops, and the TP/FP/FN color legend is adjacent to those crops.
The top research-direction strip explicitly calls segmentation robustness an “independent visual failure analysis,” making the workstream transition visible without asserting causality.
item_reviews.summary: Semantically coherent medical-image comparison with a clearly marked independent workstream transition.

observations: Across the rendered sequence, the composition alternates between formula, multi-panel line plot, design schematic, grouped bar chart, decision-flow graphic, and medical-image comparison; it is not a repeated one-template deck.
The clustered-calibration sequence has an evident model → result → design → failure → next-experiment rhythm.
The final segmentation page is visually and textually marked as an independent research direction, providing a balanced workstream transition.

The cover thumbnail visibly uses the audience-facing title “Synthetic Semantic-Alias Research Presentation Stress Deck,” which reads as test/benchmark terminology rather than a normal doctoral-group research-deck title.
item_reviews.summary: The slide rhythm, object alternation, and workstream continuity are strong, but the visible cover title leaks benchmark/test-style terminology.

non_blocking_notes: The final independent segmentation workstream is visually well differentiated while retaining the same CUHK visual system.
Several explanatory paragraphs and minor annotations are smaller than the main plots/diagrams, but the principal scientific objects remain readable in the rendered full-page views.
